notes:
Maintainer risk: LOW — bench file and example are well-isolated dev-only additions; the two P1 risks are about contributor-copy patterns and CI-gate coverage of fixture invariants, neither of which can ship a runtime defect to users.
Confidence: 5% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: none. Uncertainty driven by: I did not run cargo bench or cargo run --example to verify the new files actually compile and execute under the workspace's current rustc 1.88 + criterion 0.8 + mime-tree 0.3.0 combination — review was source-reading only per the read-only review policy. Would raise confidence if: a downstream /do-beads session ran 'cargo bench -p jmap-mime --no-run' and 'cargo build -p jmap-mime --example parse_eml' and reported zero compile errors. The src/lib.rs adapter code is unchanged in scope, so RFC-conformance correctness of the size-field-encodes-vs-decoded behavior is a pre-existing concern, not a finding of this review.
API contract risk: MEDIUM — the public API surface (src/lib.rs) is unchanged in scope, but the newly-rewritten README and the new example bake in two contract subtleties that consumers will not see: blob_id_for must be idempotent across multiple calls per leaf (or the same partId surfaces under multiple distinct blobIds on the wire), and body_value_part_ids is concatenation not union so callers iterating naively decode duplicates for the most common plain-text email shape. Both gaps are latent in the unchanged code; what makes them MEDIUM rather than LOW is that this diff adds caller-facing docs and an example that demonstrate the safe patterns without flagging the requirements, so a copy-paste-then-customise consumer has no signal.
API contract confidence: 10% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: whether jmap_types::Id::from() validates its input — if mime-tree generates part_id values containing characters disallowed by RFC 8620 §1.2 (e.g. RFC 2046-style nested ids like '1.2'), the example's Id::from(format!("blob-{}", part.part_id)) blob-id construction could panic or produce malformed Ids, which would be a related contract gap I did not trace. Uncertainty driven by: did not read jmap_types::Id::from() source, did not exhaustively map mime_tree's part_id format vocabulary; review was source-reading of the diff plus targeted trace of the unchanged message_to_jmap_body call graph. Would raise confidence if: a downstream /do-beads session ran 'cargo run --example parse_eml -p jmap-mime' against a nested multipart fixture (e.g. multipart/mixed wrapping multipart/alternative) and reported no Id-construction panic.
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — four idiomatic-Rust findings filed (t307.11 format_push_string in bench builders; t307.12 uninlined_format_args across bench+example; t307.13 loop+match-Option should be while let in assert_large_fixture; t307.14 missing trailing ; on b.iter tail expressions). All four are clippy-pedantic-grade and mechanical to fix; none reveal a structural Rust-idiom problem with the diff. src/lib.rs adapter is unchanged in scope so no idiom findings there. No unsafe, no #[derive] gaps, no lifetime smells, no error-handling smells beyond what JMAP-t307.2 (my-oss pass) already covers. A serious Rust practitioner reads the diff and nods through the example structure but reaches for clippy-fix on the bench file.
Rust idiom confidence: 8% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: none — every finding has a clippy lint or textbook idiom replacement backing it. Uncertainty driven by: did not run cargo clippy with bleeding-edge nursery lints enabled (only pedantic), so a stylistic finding from a more aggressive lint set could be missed; did not read jmap_types::Id::from() to verify the Id-construction patterns in bench loops have no panic surface (covered structurally by JMAP-t307 API-contract-risk note); did not exercise the bench file with rustc nightly to surface drop-order or temporary-lifetime warnings the stable compiler does not emit. Would raise confidence if: cargo +nightly clippy -p jmap-mime --benches --examples -- -W clippy::all -W clippy::pedantic -W clippy::nursery -W clippy::cargo reported only the four issues already filed.
Second /review-rusty pass on same scope (9c0d34f..HEAD, crate-jmap-mime/): no additional findings beyond t307.11–t307.14 from the prior pass. Re-scanned benches/mime_pipeline.rs and examples/parse_eml.rs for non-overlapping idiom issues (ownership, type design, missing trait impls, lifetime over-annotation, unsafe, additional clippy-grade patterns). Candidates considered and rejected as bikeshedding: '1usize' suffix on depth counter, '.iter()' vs '.into_iter()' on array literal, '&[String]' vs '&[&str]' parameter on write_level. None survive an engineering-basis test. Per AGENTS.md convergence rule: prior pass produced only P1+P2 mechanical-fix findings with 8% missed-issue confidence; second pass finds nothing new; idiom track has converged. Idiom rating remains ACCEPTABLE. Recommend stopping the review loop on this epic.
Third /review-rusty pass on same scope (9c0d34f..HEAD, crate-jmap-mime/): no new findings. Scope unchanged since the second pass (HEAD advanced on unrelated paths only — verified via 'git log 9c0d34f..HEAD -- crate-jmap-mime/'). The four idiom findings t307.11-t307.14 still cover the only non-bikeshedding rust-idiom issues in the diff. Per AGENTS.md convergence rule and the second pass's recommendation to stop, the idiom track has converged. Idiom rating remains ACCEPTABLE. Stopping the review-rusty loop on this epic. Filing fabricated findings to fill a third pass would be the exact bikeshedding failure mode AGENTS.md warns against. Confidence: 5% chance of missed idiom issue. No reduction below the second pass's 8% because (a) source unchanged and (b) the only way to drive this lower is the cargo +nightly clippy probe already recommended in the second-pass note, which is a /do-beads task not a /review-rusty task.
